analysis.answer: Current law requires a voter to state their name and address and sign the poll book to vote. The proposed law changes this by requiring a current government-issued photo identification.

Voters without ID incur time and transportation costs to obtain one or to visit the county clerk post-election. Counties will incur administrative costs to process, track, and verify provisional ballots.
Voters who do not currently possess a valid government-issued photo ID—often lower-income, younger, and elderly individuals—bear the primary cost of compliance.

The measure addresses ballot verification by requiring photo ID. The mechanism requires identification at the polls to prevent in-person voter impersonation, a crime that historical data indicates is extremely rare.

The effect on voter turnout is empirically disputed. Some researchers find that strict photo ID requirements disproportionately decrease turnout among minority, low-income, and young voters, while other studies find no significant effect on overall turnout.
